exams.title: Python OOP Comprehensive Assignment and Project Workbook
exams.subtitle: Concept Practice + Capstone Project

sections.title: Section A: OOP Foundations (Concept + Basic Implementation)

questions.text: Define class and object with one real-world example. Then create a class Student with attributes name and roll_no, and print two objects.
Differentiate instance variable and class variable. Write a class Employee where company is shared and emp_id is unique per object.
Write a class Rectangle with methods area() and perimeter(). Create three objects and display results in a formatted table.
Explain constructor (__init__) and object initialization. Implement a class BankAccount that validates opening balance (non-negative).
Implement instance method, class method, and static method in one class TemperatureConverter with suitable use cases.

sections.title: Section B: Encapsulation, Properties, and Data Safety

questions.text: Explain encapsulation in Python. Create a class Wallet with private balance, and methods deposit(), withdraw(), and get_balance().
Use @property and @setter in a class Product for price so that negative values are rejected with ValueError.
Design a class UserProfile where email is validated before assignment. Use property-based validation and custom error messages.
Create a class AttendanceTracker that stores attendance safely and exposes only controlled update methods (no direct list mutation).
Build a class InventoryItem with stock update methods and exception handling for invalid operations (e.g., reducing below zero).
Demonstrate single inheritance using classes Vehicle and Car. Override one method and use super() properly.
Demonstrate multilevel inheritance with classes Person -> Employee -> Manager and show constructor chaining.
Create a multiple-inheritance example with classes Camera, Phone, and SmartPhone. Explain MRO with output.
Implement runtime polymorphism: create classes Circle and Rectangle with a common method area(), and process them in one loop.
Write a duck-typing example where unrelated classes implement send() and a notifier function works with all of them.

sections.title: Section D: Abstraction and Magic Methods

questions.text: Use abc.ABC to define an abstract class Shape with abstract methods area() and perimeter(). Implement for Triangle and Square.
Create a class Book and implement __str__ and __repr__. Explain where each is used with sample output.
Create a class Vector2D and overload + and == operators using __add__ and __eq__.
Implement __len__ for a custom Playlist class and show how len(obj) can be used meaningfully.
Build a class Logger with context-manager support (__enter__, __exit__) to write start/end session logs to a file.

sections.title: Section E: Capstone Project (Integrating All OOP Topics)

questions.text: Build one complete mini-project in Python (for example: Library Management, Expense Tracker, or Course Enrollment System) using OOP. Your solution must demonstrate classes/objects, encapsulation with property validation, inheritance and method overriding, polymorphism, at least two magic methods, composition, exception handling, and clear module-level structure. Submit source code, sample input/output, and a short design note explaining class relationships.
